title: How To Increase Student Online Participation By 50 Percent n-by-50-percent/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: For students who have gone entirely dark on remote learning, Linsin argues the most effective lever is bypassing parents and speaking to the student directly by phone, since parents often lack the leverage or resolve to compel engagement themselves. He provides a short, direct script that tells the student clearly what is expected, asks if any obstacle is in the way, and ends the call without soliciting reassurances that may not be sincere. He credits the approach with getting up to fifty percent more disengaged students back to work, attributing its effectiveness to the direct relational leverage of the Law of Reciprocity between a well-liked teacher and student. He recommends keeping a running list of students to call weekly and pairing the calls with full grace — allowing prior work to be turned in penalty-free — since many students are still developing the self-starter skills required for remote learning.
points: Bypass parents and call disengaged students directly; parents often lack the leverage to compel engagement themselves.
Use a short, direct script that states expectations clearly and asks about obstacles, without soliciting reassurances.
This direct-contact approach produced up to 50% more re-engagement among previously disengaged students.
Keep a running weekly list of students to call who missed lessons or assignments the previous week.
Pair direct calls with full grace — allowing prior work to be submitted penalty-free — since many students are still learning self-starter skills.
quotes: A few of which have been entirely off the grid for the past two months, whereabouts unknown.
Sorry, but if a family has internet access and the child is on TikTok and watching Netflix instead of doing their school work, then the parents aren’t doing their job.
Here at SCM, our team has had success getting more students involved and doing their work—up to 50% more—by speaking directly to the student.
It’s important that you don’t ask for assurances . You’re using your position as their teacher as leverage to get them moving, and thus you must tell them what they need to do.
Nearly every student we were able to talk to ended up turning in work within a day. And here’s the best part: They didn’t backslide.

In other words, give your students a chance to complete all previous assignments with no penalty. This is a tough time and many are just acquiring the self-starter skills they need to learn from home.
